back: E.m.f. of a half-cell connected to a standard hydrogen electrode under standard conditions (298 K, 101 kPa, 1.00 mol dm⁻³), written for the reduction.
H₂ at 101 kPa over platinum (black) in 1.00 mol dm⁻³ H⁺(aq) at 298 K; E⦵ = 0.00 V.
E⦵cell = E⦵(positive electrode) − E⦵(negative electrode); never multiply E⦵ by coefficients.
More positive E⦵: stronger oxidising agent (left side). More negative E⦵: stronger reducing agent (right side).
Feasible under standard conditions if E⦵(species reduced) − E⦵(species oxidised) is positive.
Filter paper soaked in saturated KNO₃: completes the circuit by ion movement without mixing solutions.
Used when no metal appears in the half-equation (Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺, Cl₂/Cl⁻, H⁺/H₂): inert conductor.
Says nothing about rate; conditions may be non-standard; products may differ.
F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂: E⦵ falls down Group 17, so each halogen oxidises the halide ions below it.
